title: Latency & Network Health Orchestrator: temporal-decay composite score for region ranking and variant fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current region selection logic uses separate percentile signals (p50/p95) and ad-hoc network flags. This ticket implements a single composite region score that fuses latency quantiles and network health signals with a temporal decay model to prefer stable, low-latency POPs while enabling graceful variant fallbacks when health degrades.

Goals:
- Produce a composite Region Health Index (RHI) in real time for each POP that combines latency (p50, p95), recent error-rate, retransmit/packet-loss proxies, and TCP connection failures.
- Use a temporal-decay EWMA to avoid flip-flopping on transient spikes while still reacting to sustained regressions.
- Provide deterministic ranking and a confidence band to drive tier routing (tiered POPs) and automated fallback to compatible model variants when RHI crosses thresholds.
- Emit explainability metadata for each decision (which signal dominated, temporal trend score) for Console and incident triage.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change model selection policies for non-latency-sensitive customers (separate follow-up).
- Not addressing cross-region data residency policies here.
acceptance_criteria: RHI computed and available via /routing/score v2 API for all POPs at 1s resolution
Ranking stable: simulated traffic replay with injected 5% and 20% packet-loss shows reasonable hysteresis (no >3 switches per 10m window)
Tier routing rules can be configured to use RHI and confidence band; default policy uses primary/secondary/tertiary POPs
Automatic selection of pre-warmed variant (smaller quantized model) when POP RHI < fallback_threshold and falls back within configured SLA budget
Documentation and console panels show signal contributions (p50, p95, error_rate, netloss proxy) and EWMA half-life used
tech_design:
Score composition:
- Inputs: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_rate_1m, conns_fail_rate_1m, net_loss_proxy_1m.
- Normalize each input to 0..100 band using running-percentile baselines per POP and model class. Baseline windows: 7d rolling for long-term baseline, 1h rolling for dynamic baseline.
- Compute quantile_gap = clamp((p95 - p50) / max(p50, 1ms), 0, 10). Map quantile_gap -> penalty term.
- RawScore = w1 * norm(p50) + w2 * norm(p95) + w3 * quantile_gap_penalty + w4 * norm(error_rate) + w5 * norm(net_loss_proxy). Default weights: w1=0.25, w2=0.35, w3=0.15, w4=0.15, w5=0.10. Weights configurable per customer tier.
- Temporal smoothing: RHI(t) = EWMA(alpha) of RawScore(t). Alpha computed from half-life H: alpha = 1 - exp(-ln(2)/H). Default H = 90s for high-sensitivity POPs and 300s for stable enterprise POPs.
- Confidence band: compute short-window variance of RawScore (30s) and expose as +/- band. Use to avoid routing decisions when confidence is low.

Fallback rules:
- If RHI_primary > fallback_threshold OR confidence indicates sustained degradation for >= degrade_window (default 60s), route to next-ranked POP.
- If ranked POPs lack capacity or RHI also degraded, route to pre-configured model variant (e.g., quantized-small) that is marked as compatible for the workload. Tag request with fallback_reason and fallback_path in trace.

Implementation notes:
- Compute RawScore at the edge-telemetry pipeline (existing Kafka topic), then aggregate and publish RHI via Redis TPU for low-latency reads by routing layer.
- All baselines and normalization tables stored in time-series (TSDB) with versioned keys so we can replay/retrospect.
- Expose /routing/score/v2 producing: pop_id, RHI_value, short_variance, contributing_signals, baseline_snapshot_id. (API contract in design doc link.)

Trade-offs considered:
- Using EWMA vs windowed median: EWMA reacts faster; windowed median more robust to outliers. Chosen EWMA with configurable half-life for tunability.
- Normalization windows: longer windows reduce churn but are slow to reflect trend shifts; we use dual baselines (7d and 1h) and prefer the 1h when drift > 30% of 7d baseline.

Security/compliance: metrics contain only aggregated telemetry; no customer PII.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement RawScore computation in telemetry-processor (feature branch) and unit tests (2 weeks). 2) Lightweight canary: publish RHI flags to a subset of traffic (5%) in staging with routing logic simulated (no live route changes) to compare decisions vs baseline (1 week). 3) Shadow routing in production (no cutover) for 2 days to validate rankings and capture mismatch rates. 4) Canary routing for 1% traffic with automatic rollback on SLO regressions (>2% p95 increase or >1% error-rate uplift). 5) Ramp 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% across 3 days with monitoring and weekly review.

Monitoring & runbook triggers:
- Alert if routing mismatch rate > 0.5% across 1h or pop switch rate > 10 switches per 10m.
- Auto-rollback if customer-visible p95 increases > 10% from baseline for > 15m.
